# Laws of the variety generated by a quasivariety

For a set $Q$ of quasi-identities of groups, the set of elements $w$ of the free group $F$ on countably many generators that are laws of every group satisfying all quasi-identities in $Q$ (every homomorphism from $F$ to such a group sends $w$ to $1$). These are the laws of the variety generated by the quasivariety defined by $Q$. A quasi-identity is a sentence $\forall x\,(w_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_k = 1 \to w = 1)$ with finitely many premises, all words in finitely many unknowns.
